$schema_note: Design tokens for the slides skill. The semantic and typography keys map to the CSS custom properties the HTML template in references/html-template.md consumes: --color-primary, --color-background, --color-secondary, --primitive-gradient-primary, --typography-font-heading, --typography-font-body. Copy the emitted block into the :root of a deck, then replace the values with the brand's.

meta.name: Default deck theme
meta.provenance: Default values. These are a starting point, not a look. A deck that ships with these tokens ships with a deck nobody chose.
meta.contrast: text on background is 15.8:1 and muted text on background is 7.1:1, both above WCAG AA for all text sizes. primary on background is 4.6:1, which clears AA for large text only: never set body copy in primary on this dark ground.

css_variables._note: Paste this block into the deck's :root. These are the exact names the HTML template and the layout patterns reference, so renaming one silently drops the styling.

type_scale._note: Modular, ratio 1.25, anchored on a 16px base. These are minimums for a 1920x1080 deck viewed at arm's length; a title smaller than 4rem is unreadable from the back of a room, and body copy smaller than 1.5rem is unreadable from a laptop.
type_scale.measure: 60ch for a body paragraph, 24ch for a headline

layout._note: Grid and safe area for a 16:9 deck. content_width is the text column; anything wider than about 24 characters per line is harder to read, not easier.
layout.safe_area: the central 80% of the canvas; platform UI and projection overscan eat the edges

chart._note: The defaults every Chart.js config in a deck should start from. A chart that does not inherit these reads as pasted in from another deck, which is exactly what it is.

motion._note: Deck transitions. Every one of these is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion, and the rule is at the bottom of the emitted block rather than in each component, because a component that forgets it is the failure mode.

rules: One idea per slide. A slide that needs two headlines is two slides.
The headline is the claim, not the topic. 'Revenue grew 3x' beats 'Revenue', and it survives being read out of context.
A number on the slide is a claim; a number on the slide with its denominator is evidence.
Body copy is a maximum, not a target. If a slide needs a paragraph, it needs a different layout.
Never put text over the busiest part of a background image. If there is nowhere clear, the image is the wrong image.
Two fonts per deck. Three is a mistake that looks like indecision.
